questions.q: What is the main indicator of lithium battery wear?
options: The cycle count written on the sticker
The color of the wrap after a flight
The battery's weight on a scale
The internal resistance of the cells
questions.explain: Rising IR means less output under load and more heating; measure it with the same device at the same temperature.
Storage is 3.80–3.85 V; don't keep them full for more than a few days.

questions.q: A prop touched the grass on landing, no visible cracks. What do you do?
options: Keep flying, since there are no cracks
Swap it with another motor's prop
questions.explain: A prop that has touched something gets replaced: microcracks are invisible, and a failure in flight means losing the aircraft.

questions.q: A motor's MTBF is 1000 h. What is the probability of running 1000 h without a failure?
Motor reliability is r. What is the quadcopter's reliability with respect to motors?
questions.explain: A series system: all four are needed, R = r⁴.

questions.q: Why doesn't a hexa always survive a motor failure?
options: Six motors are heavier than four
A motor failure is not dangerous for a hexa at all
It depends on the frame, thrust and firmware
questions.explain: The ability to make it home on five motors is tested, not assumed.

questions.q: Vibration grows from flight to flight with the same props. Likely cause?
options: Cold weather on the day of the flight
questions.explain: A vibration trend is an early sign of bearing wear and loosened mounts.

questions.q: What does the bathtub curve give you for operations?
options: A reason not to replace components until the first failure
Acceptance testing of new units and replacement by service life
questions.explain: Early failures are caught by acceptance testing, wear-out by replacement before its zone.
